title: The Construction of an AI-based chatbot to Provide Formative Feedback on Argumentative Writing
abstract: The study explores students’ perceptions of the efficacy of an AI-based chatbot "IELTS Writing Tutor" in providing formative feedback on argumentative essays to first-year engineering students at a China-UK collaborative undergraduate program. Built on the Smartutor platform, the chatbot delivers structured feedback aligned with IELTS Writing Task 2 criteria, model answers, and reflection prompts. 29 students engaged in the research and received feedback on the three writing responses they wrote. This study employed a mixed-methods approach. Quantitative data were collected via a 5-point Likert scale questionnaire measuring perceived usefulness and ease of use of the chatbot, followed by SPSS-based descriptive analysis. Qualitative data included open-ended feedback from students, which was analyzed using thematic analysis. The study found participants rated the chatbot highly on both usefulness and ease of use, with all mean scores exceeding 4.2. While its core strengths are recognized in promptly identifying errors and delivering learning-focused feedback, the findings indicate that future development must focus on two key areas: advancing personalized learning experience and diversifying modes of interaction.

title: Design and Implementation of a Lattice-Based Post-Quantum Secure Bootloader for RISC-V with QEMU-Based Validation
abstract: The rapid proliferation of RISC-V architectures in embedded, IoT, and safety-critical systems necessitates quantum-resistant secure boot mechanisms to counter harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks targeting classical RSA/ECDSA firmware signatures. This paper presents PQBoot-C, a complete 52 kB production-ready C implementation of a lattice-based post-quantum secure bootloader for RISC-V 64-bit processors featuring NIST-standardized Dilithium2 (ML-DSA) signature verification. PQBoot-C establishes a quantum-resilient hardware root-of-trust through a multi-stage PQChain verification protocol: SHA3-256 measured boot computes kernel integrity, Dilithium2 authenticates firmware against an embedded public key, and Physical Memory Protection (PMP) enforces hardware-isolated execution. Comprehensive QEMU RV64GCV emulation enables reproducible cycle-accurate profiling, demonstrating a bounded total secure boot cost of 1.43 million clock cycles, corresponding to 14.3 ms on a 100 MHz core and 1.43 ms on a 1 GHz core.Cross-platform validation confirms deployment readiness across QEMU virt, VisionFive2, and HiFive Unmatched platforms, with deterministic execution and full UART traceability. Security analysis demonstrates 128-bit IND-CCA quantum resistance with tamper-evident logging and constant-time Dilithium2 via masked pqm4 integration. The crypto-agile design supports future PQC migration (Falcon, SPHINCS+) while maintaining a sub-100 kB footprint suitable for resource-constrained embedded deployment. PQBoot-C provides the first open-source, QEMU-reproducible baseline for post-quantum RISC-V secure boot, bridging the critical research-to-deployment gap.

title: From Actions to Understanding: Conformal Interpretability of Temporal Concepts in LLM Agents
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents capable of reasoning, planning, and acting within interactive environments. Despite their growing capability to perform multi-step reasoning and decision-making tasks, internal mechanisms guiding their sequential behavior remain opaque. This paper presents a framework for interpreting the temporal evolution of concepts in LLM agents through a step-wise conformal lens. We introduce the conformal interpretability framework for temporal tasks, which combines step-wise reward modeling with conformal prediction to statistically label model's internal representation at each step as successful or failing. Linear probes are then trained on these representations to identify directions of temporal concepts - latent directions in the model's activation space that correspond to consistent notions of success, failure or reasoning drift. Experimental results on two simulated interactive environments, namely ScienceWorld and AlfWorld, demonstrate that these temporal concepts are linearly separable, revealing interpretable structures aligned with task success. We further show preliminary results on improving an LLM agent's performance by leveraging the proposed framework for steering the identified successful directions inside the model. The proposed approach, thus, offers a principled method for early failure detection as well as intervention in LLM-based agents, paving the path towards trustworthy autonomous language models in complex interactive settings.

title: A new approach to rating scale definition with quantum-inspired optimization
abstract: In finance, assessing the creditworthiness of loan applicants requires lenders to cluster borrowers using rating scales. Financial institutions must define the scales in compliance with strict institutional constraints, resulting in solving a complex combinatorial constrained optimization problem. This contribution studies how to solve this problem using a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) model, a formulation suitable for quantum hardware. We validate this approach by testing the proposed formulation with classical heuristics. We then benchmark the results against a brute-force method to demonstrate consistent solution quality and highlight the framework's suitability for more complex scenarios.

title: Human-AI Co-authoring for Personalized Practice With Multilayer Graph
abstract: This paper presents a proof-of-concept for a scalable approach to personalized learning that generates practice questions aligned to intended practice targets, controlling for question complexity. The focus is to provide learner-centered scaffolding in preparation for assessments by generating questions that align learner topic proficiency with targeted complexity. Historical assessment items are transformed into a topic-linked representation by multi-labeling each question with topics from a predefined syllabus. The labeling is produced by employing a previously built prompt-engineered GPT-5 model configuration with retrieval augmented generation. Topic labels are combined with student performance traces to derive personalized topic-level proficiency proxies. We then build a multilayer graph based on conceptual hierarchy and historical co-assessment. Querying the multilayer graph retrieves coherent topic sets around a student's priority topics based on learning needs, supporting content selection that is both topically consistent and conceptually coherent. A prompt-engineered GPT-5 model then generates questions for an inferred SOLO taxonomy level based on a learner's profile (proficiency and residue), conditioned on the retrieved topic sets. Outputs are evaluated for SOLO alignment and profile calibration through expert review, showing a high level of agreement. This methodology offers a pathway to operationalizing human-AI collaboration for adaptive practice, enabling scalable, varied revision for learners.

title: Research on Student Psychological Analysis Method Based on Particle Swarm Optimization and K-means Clustering Algorithm
abstract: Traditional student psychological analysis methods exhibit significant shortcomings, characterized by high subjectivity and insufficient clustering accuracy and global optimization capabilities. To address these issues, this paper proposes a student psychological analysis solution integrating Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and K-means clustering. University students were selected as research subjects, with core psychological indicators collected and standardized to construct a dataset. To mitigate the deficiency of K-means' random initial cluster center selection, the PSO algorithm was introduced to optimize this key parameter. By combining Euclidean distance, the clustering similarity measurement method was improved, resulting in a PSO-K-means hybrid algorithm. Comparative experiments validated the algorithm's practical effectiveness, employing multiple evaluation metrics to assess its performance. The results demonstrate that this hybrid algorithm can accurately classify student psychological states, providing reliable technical support for psychological intervention efforts in universities.

title: Anomaly Detection for Circuit Waveforms Using Diffusion Model
abstract: Circuit waveform inspection is critical to ensuring performance and reliability in consumer electronic products. However, engineers in industrial production lines often inspect waveforms manually, requiring technical expertise and time. To automate and speed up testing, we propose a diffusion model based normal waveform generator (DNWG) that reconstructs waveform images using only normal data, eliminating abnormal sample collection and retraining for unknown anomalies. By integrating masking techniques to preserve output accuracy, DNWG enables anomaly detection for previously unseen issues. In addition, we introduce the compositional similarity index, which considers the electrical and physical properties of circuits, improving upon conventional similarity metrics. This approach increases efficiency for anomaly detection in circuit waveform inspection.

title: Novel Machine Learning and Quantum Computing for Audio Biometrics: Deep Audio Feature Analysis and Speech Patterns for Real-Time Authentication Systems
abstract: Biometric authentication is essential for secure identity management in the age of digital services and ecosystems. Audio-based authentication outperforms other biometric methods due to its ease of use and compatibility with most devices. Most audio biometric systems have background noise, deception, and real-time use. A new quantum computing-ML architecture improves deep audio feature analysis and speech pattern recognition for real-time authentication systems. Deep learning and quantum physics provide accurate, high-dimensional speech data representations. Recurrent and convolutional neural networks identify audio patterns. We can adjust to various expressions since we can focus on one task. Quantum kernel estimation and variational quantum circuits trump basic machine learning. They protect the system from outside influences and threats, enabling its widespread acceptance. Edge computing lets lowresource devices learn and judge quickly, enabling real-time authentication. Quantum anomaly detection reduces replay attacks, vocal changes, and deepfake speech. Real and virtual acoustic testing have deeper accuracy, FAR, and FRR. A novel audio authentication biometrics solution uses machine learning and quantum computing. The findings show that query language and machine learning frameworks can overcome security, robustness, and scalability challenges. Voice interfaces and audio-driven technology are growing in consumer electronics, finance, and infrastructure. Safe, effective, and future-proof identity verification is achieved with this method.

title: Quantum-Inspired approaches to Multi-robot Scheduling and Control using QAOA and VQE
abstract: Quantum computation injection into robot automation opens up new avenues for boosting multi-robot complicated task scheduling and real-time adaptive control. Conventional optimization methods barely keep up with the challenges of scalability and efficiency in dynamic environments, thus becoming one of the bottlenecks for successful robotic coordination. This paper puts forward two leading quantum algorithms, Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) and Variational Quantum Eigen solver (VQE), as a remedy to these shortcomings. Through the use of quantum parallelism and hybrid quantum-classical architectures, the intended solution is to elevate task assignment effectiveness and interactive response capacity in multi-robotic systems. Among other things, the proposed work aims at setting up a quantum inspired optimization model to schedule a task, an adaptive and real-time decision-support control framework, and the experimental demonstration of the algorithm's capability to handle complexity and high volume in robotic environments. Computer-based simulations alongside actual experiments, as a matter of fact, will be able to outperform regular optimizations, hence proving the transformative potentials of quantum algorithms on robotic automation.

title: CoAuthorAI: A Human in the Loop System For Scientific Book Writing
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in scientific writing but struggle with book-length tasks, often producing inconsistent structure and unreliable citations. We introduce CoAuthorAI, a human-in-the-loop writing system that combines retrieval-augmented generation, expert-designed hierarchical outlines, and automatic reference linking. The system allows experts to iteratively refine text at the sentence level, ensuring coherence and accuracy. In evaluations of 500 multi-domain literature review chapters, CoAuthorAI achieved a maximum soft-heading recall of 98%; in a human evaluation of 100 articles, the generated content reached a satisfaction rate of 82%. The book AI for Rock Dynamics generated with CoAuthorAI and Kexin Technology's LUFFA AI model has been published with Springer Nature. These results show that systematic human-AI collaboration can extend LLMs' capabilities from articles to full-length books, enabling faster and more reliable scientific publishing.

title: Improved Approximation Algorithms and Hardness Results for Shortest Common Superstring with Reverse Complements
abstract: The Shortest Common Superstring (SCS) problem is a fundamental task in sequence analysis. In genome assembly, however, the double-stranded nature of DNA implies that each fragment may occur either in its original orientation or as its reverse complement. This motivates the Shortest Common Superstring with Reverse Complements (SCS-RC) problem, which asks for a shortest string that contains, for each input string, either the string itself or its reverse complement as a substring. The previously best-known approximation ratio for SCS-RC was $\frac{23}{8}$. In this paper, we present a new approximation algorithm achieving an improved ratio of $\frac{8}{3}$. Our approach computes an optimal constrained cycle cover by reducing the problem, via a novel gadget construction, to a maximum-weight perfect matching in a general graph. We also investigate the computational hardness of SCS-RC. While the decision version is known to be NP-complete, no explicit inapproximability results were previously established. We show that the hardness of SCS carries over to SCS-RC through a polynomial-time reduction, implying that it is NP-hard to approximate SCS-RC within a factor better than $\frac{333}{332}$. Notably, this hardness result holds even for the DNA alphabet.

title: Reasoning About the Non-Existent in Large Language Models: Benchmark Success, Negation Failure, and Exploratory Creativity
abstract: Can artificial intelligence reason about things that do not exist, are not true, or are merely hypothetical? This paper addresses these questions with a two-part analysis of non-existence reasoning in state-of-the-art large language models. The analysis includes four components: counterfactual inference, negation handling, creative novelty, and multi-turn persistence of imaginary knowledge. Part 1 uses a benchmark-calibrated forecasting model to predict future performance for 12 models on 15,300 simulated datapoints. Part 2 revisits the question with live API evaluations of 5 state-of-the-art models on over 654 items covering CRASS-style counterfactual questions, negation tasks, creativity prompts, and multi-turn dialogues about imaginary topics. The outcome is a differentiated capability profile rather than a simple yes or no answer to the question of whether AI can reason about non-existence. The sampled CRASS items produced near-ceiling performance relative to the published human baseline, suggesting that some portions of the benchmark may no longer provide strong discriminative power among state-of-the-art models. By contrast, negation was associated with statistically significant performance drops in the four complete model runs, with the same directional tendency also visible in the partial fifth run. The conclusions about creative novelty and multi-turn imaginary persistence are more provisional since they rested on proxy measures and heuristic contradiction detection. In substance, the results imply that top models can execute certain types of structured counterfactual reasoning effectively but display a robust and replicable deficit with respect to negation; indications of difficulty with creative novelty and multi-turn imaginative persistence are present but rest on weaker proxy measures and should be treated as provisional. In method, they underscore the importance of treating benchmark-calibrated forecasts as perishable hypotheses that must be revalidated with live model evaluations in a rapidly evolving LLM environment.

ケース・スタディ資料(物語形式)は、どの業界の企業経営に適用するのかによって、工夫すべき点が業界ごとに異なる。とくに、入力データの収集とデータ間の関係の調整(名寄せ・時系列の粒度や分類の粒度の共通化、単位の異なるデータを比較可能にするための統計的な標準化など)は、それぞれの業界ごとに、データセットの特徴が大きく異なることから、業界の違いを越えた画一的なデータ前処理工程の王道は存在しない。そのため、各業界別に、ケース・スタディ資料を作成する方針を取っている。 このガイドブックは、民間航空会社を取り扱っている(これまでのシリーズでは、繊維製造メーカー企業、ゼネコン企業、半導体製造企業を対象とした『ジオメトリック・インテリジェンス』導入解説を行ってきた)。 ストーリーの概要と本書の設定を選んだ理由 舞台は2031年。日本の国家安全保障局(NSS)から天翔航空に対し、特定の外交的貨物を72時間以内にロンドン・ヒースロー空港まで輸送するよう要請が下る。しかし、①ロシアのウクライナ侵攻以来続くシベリア上空の閉鎖(欧米・日本・カナダの航空会社に対する報復的なOverflight Permit撤回)、②台湾海峡をめぐる緊張による中国FIRの段階的な通過制限強化、③フーシ派(イエメン武装勢力)による紅海沿岸の対空ミサイル・ドローン脅威——という三つの独立した禁止区域が、東京・ロンドン間のいかなる通常航路も遮断していた。残された選択肢は、北極海を経由する非標準航路のみであった。 この設定は、現在進行中の地政学的リスクを忠実に反映している。1944年のシカゴ条約第1条は「各国はその領土の上空において完全かつ排他的な主権を有する」と定め、第9条は緊急時に即座の飛行禁止措置を認める。制度の枠組みは80年近く変わっていないが、①この主権を行使する主体の多様化(国家から非国家主体であるフーシ派まで)、②政治的報復手段としての領空閉鎖の常態化、③国際条約の外側から来る非対称な脅威の出現——という三重の変化が重なり、民間航空会社が運航継続のために直面する制約の複雑さは質的に変容した。 本書は、この複雑さを「飛行可能な空域全体を底空間Bとしたとき、三つの独立した禁止区域が底空間に三つの穴を開け、第1コホモロジー群H¹(B, F)が非自明となる」という位相幾何学の言語で正確に記述し、それを数学的に解く物語として構成されている。地政学的リスクを、現場の意思決定者が運用できる数学的枠組みへと橋渡しすることが、本書の中心的な問いである。 GI理論を民間航空便の運航に適用する場合の特徴 航空データセットの特性——他産業との比較 航空業界のデータセットが他産業と異なる最大の特徴は、風(ジェット気流)が計量そのものを非対称にするという点にある。製造業や海運業では、環境要因は外生的なノイズとして扱える場合が多い。しかし航空では、同一区間を東方向に飛ぶ場合と西方向に飛ぶ場合とで飛行時間が2〜3時間異なる。これは「距離」の概念が対称性を失うことを意味しており、標準的なリーマン計量(方向非依存の距離)では現実を正確に記述できない。 本書で用いたのはフィンスラー計量のランダー型F = α + β(Randers metric)である。αは背景のリーマン計量(風のない場合の距離)、βはジェット気流を表す1-形式(飛行方向に応じて符号が変わる非対称な補正項)であり、その和Fが「風の中を飛ぶ航空機の実際の距離感覚」を記述する。ランダー計量はツェルメロの航法問題(風の中での最適航法の数学的定式化)と等価であることが証明されており、航空運航の物理を最も自然に記述する計量クラスである。 また、航空データは**ADS-B(Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast)**という、航空機自身がGPSから計算した位置・速度・高度を1090MHz帯で自動送信するシステムによって継続的に蓄積されている。本書では東京発ロンドン着の過去5年分の全フライト(23,847件)のADS-Bデータを使用した。製造業の生産ラインデータや海運の航行ログとは異なり、このデータには「風速ベクトルの直接観測値」が内包されている:真対気速度(TAS)と対地速度(GS)の差分が、そのままβ項の推定値となる。これは他産業にはない航空データ特有の性質であり、外生的な気象予報に頼ることなく、実フライトデータそのものから計量を学習できる。 GI理論の三条件(命題1.1)を航空データで充足するための工夫 GI Vol.1 命題1.1は、VAE(変分自己符号化器)から可微分多様体を構築するために以下の三条件を要求する。 条件(i):VAEデコーダのC³級滑らかさ 活性化関数の選択が鍵となる。航空多様体では高度・速度・位置の急激な変化を扱うため、ReLU(折れ曲がり点で1階微分が不連続)は使用できない。全層にtanh(双曲線正接関数、C∞級)を使用することで、測地線方程式が要求するクリストッフェル記号の計算に必要な2階微分の連続性を保証した。 条件(ii):ヤコビ行列のフルランク VAE訓練後にデコーダのヤコビ行列のSVD(特異値分解)を実施し、最小特異値0.312(ゼロから十分離れている)を確認した。また、KNN(k近傍)保存率0.891(目標値0.85以上)により、潜在空間の幾何学が実フライトデータの多様体構造を忠実に反映していることを検証した。 条件(iii):ランダー条件 ‖β‖_α < 1 この条件は「風速が航空機の真対気速度を超えない」という物理的条件と等価である。787-9のTAS(約250 m/s、マッハ0.85)に対し、北太平洋のジェット気流は典型的に50〜100 m/s(最大値で約0.40の比率)であり、条件は全区間で満たされた。実測値は出発時0.38、飛行中最大0.56であった。なお、0.65を超えると時変フィンスラー計量の理論的安定性が保証されなくなることから、超過時にはリーマン計量へのフォールバックを設計段階から組み込んだ。この「理論の限界を正直に設計する」姿勢は、航空安全(DO-178C)との整合性の観点からも不可欠である。 このほか、GFS・ECMWFの気象予報モデルとADS-Bの実測値を統合した二重データソース構造により、β項の推定誤差を±0.04以内に抑え、通信途絶時でも機上Embodied Agentが最後の既知計量から局所的に更新を継続できるアーキテクチャを採用した。 本書の読者へのメッセージ 本書が描く世界では、一人のエンジニア(カイト)が「今まで数学と物理とプログラミングだけ学んできた。でも今回の一件に参加してから、国際政治と法律を本腰入れて学ばなきゃと思っている」と語る場面がある。これは、GI理論の実践者に求められる知識の横断性を象徴している。 航空運航にGI理論を適用するためには、以下が同時に必要である。 数学の知識——フィンスラー幾何学(ランダー計量・チャーン接続・測地線方程式)、位相幾何学(コホモロジー群、ジグザグ・パーシステンス)、最適制御理論(ポントリャーギンの最大原理・随伴変数)、情報幾何学(フィッシャー情報量計量・VAE引き戻し計量)が、互いに接続した一つの体系として使いこなせること。本書に登場する数学は、それぞれ独立した分野として一流大学の大学院レベルで教えられているが、それらを横断するカリキュラムは2026年現在、世界のどこにも存在しない。 コード実装とAIアルゴリズムの知見——VAEの訓練ループとC³条件を満たすアーキテクチャ設計、フィンスラー測地線の数値解法(約40秒で再計算できる実装)、14体のAI Agentの並列設計と通信プロトコル、形式検証ツール(Lean 4)とZKML(ゼロ知識証明による機械学習の計算検証)の組み合わせ。理論を「動く実装」に落とし込む工学的知見が不可欠である。 地政学と国際法の知識——シカゴ条約の条文、二国間航空協定の枠組み、非国家主体が生み出す法の外側のリスク、制裁リスト(OFAC・EU・国連)のリアルタイム監視。数学が設計した航路が「法的に飛べるか」を判断するためには、これらを数式と同じ精度で理解する必要がある。数学が地形を設計し、法律と国際政治がその地形の制約を決める。 判断力と勇気——本書の核心的な問いは「測地線を信じますか」という一言に集約される。数学的に最適な経路が存在すると証明されても、通信が途絶した北極海上空でロシア領空の12海里以内まで接近するか否かの最終判断は、機長が下す。AIは測地線を計算し、人間が決断する。理論の限界を正直に認識した上で、不完全な情報のもとで行動する意志——これが、GI理論の実践者に求められる最後の、そして最も重要な条件である。 GI理論は「一人の天才が全部わかる」ことを前提としない。数学者・エンジニア・パイロット・ディスパッチャー・アクチュアリー・地政学アナリストが、同じ数学的言語で対話できるチームを前提としている。本書は、そのチームがどのように機能するかの具体的な描写でもある。 なぜ航空業界にはGIを用いた統合リスク管理が不可欠なのか 航空業界が直面するリスクは、他産業と比較して以下の三点で構造的に異なる。 第一に、リスクの同時多発性と相互依存性。本書が描くように、気象リスク(ジェット気流の予報外れ)・運航安全リスク(ETOPSの制約)・地政学的リスク(FIRの閉鎖)・保険リスク(戦争リスク条項)・通信リスク(太陽フレアによる電離層障害)が12時間のフライト中に同時に発生し、かつ相互に依存する。ETOPS代替空港の気象悪化が保険ファイバーのH¹を変化させ、それがルート変更の可否に影響する。これらを個別に管理するサイロ型リスク管理は、構造的に破綻する。 第二に、リアルタイム性の要求。航空機は時速900 km で飛行している。地政学的な情勢変化(NOTAMによる空域制限の発出)から気象の急変まで、判断のサイクルタイムは分単位である。経営会議で半期に一度リスクを審議するような産業とは根本的に異なる。GI理論が採用する「測地線のリアルタイム再計算(約40秒)と14体のAI Agentによる並列監視」は、この要求に対応する設計である。 第三に、「通常の経路が存在しない」状況への対応。従来の航路最適化は「既存の航空路の中からどれを選ぶか」という選択問題を前提としてきた。しかし、地政学的緊張が高まり複数の大国が同時期に領空を閉鎖する現代では、既存のどの航空路も選択できない状況——本書でいうH¹(B, F) ≠ 0の状態——が現実のシナリオとして生じうる。この場合に必要なのは「新しい測地線を設計する数学」であり、従来のグリッド探索アルゴリズムでは対応できない。ランダー計量上の連続的な測地線方程式を解く能力は、まさにこの「通常の経路が存在しない」局面のためにある。 さらに、航空業界は乗客の生命安全という最高度の責任を負う。DO-178C(航空電子機器ソフトウェア安全基準)との整合、ETOPS認証要件、各国航空当局への説明責任——これらを充足しながらAIシステムを運航に組み込む際には、「数学的に正しいことと、航空安全として正しいことは別の概念」(本書第15章、CTO ヨルゲンの言葉)という緊張を常に意識する必要がある。ZKMLによる計算の形式検証と、パイロットの最終判断権限の明示的な保持が、この緊張を解消する設計原則となる。 GI Ver.3への展望 本書(GIケーススタディ第11作、航空産業編)は、GI Vol.3の数学的素材を先取りする形で設計されている。 GI Vol.1(リーマン計量・フィンスラー計量・H¹コホモロジー・VAE引き戻し計量)とGI Vol.2(シンプレクティック幾何・ワイル幾何・ジグザグ・パーシステンス・AI Agent設計)で確立した枠組みを、本書は航空という極限状況のもとで実証した。北太平洋でのリアルタイムβ項更新、北極海での通信途絶時11分間の自律運用、二つのコホモロジー問題の同時発生(ETOPS穴と保険穴)、極渦による計量急変時のリーマンへのフォールバックと時変フィンスラー計量の未解決問題——これらは、GI Vol.3が扱うべき数学的課題を実データから照射している。 GI Vol.3では次の数学領域の統合を予定している:シンプレクティック積分法の長期安定シミュレーションへの応用(エネルギー保存と構造保存)、ワイル幾何のゲージ不変性をAI出力検証に適用するフレームワーク、情報幾何学(フィッシャー情報量計量)によるSIGINT異常検知との接続、最適輸送理論(ワッサースタイン計量)による確率分布の時間変化追跡、双曲幾何(ポアンカレ埋め込み)による組織・ネットワーク構造の表現。 本書の後日談(第16章)では、天翔航空の航空多様体と曙海運の海上多様体の統合構想——海と空が同じ数学的言語で動く日本発の地理情報多様体インフラ——が語られる。これがGIケーススタディ第12作(海運産業編)へと引き継がれ、GI Vol.3の理論的裏付けとなる予定である。 GI理論が目指すのは「数学と、法律と、地政学と、工学が交差する場所に立てる人間が設計するシステム」である。その交差点は、2026年現在、世界のどの大学のカリキュラムにも存在しない。本ケーススタディシリーズが、その交差点を実践の場から構築するための素材となることを期待する。

Surveillance-Broadcast)**という、航空機自身がGPSから計算した位置・速度・高度を1090MHz帯で自動送信するシステムによって継続的に蓄積されている。本書では東京発ロンドン着の過去5年分の全フライト(23,847件)のADS-Bデータを使用した。製造業の生産ラインデータや海運の航行ログとは異なり、このデータには「風速ベクトルの直接観測値」が内包されている:真対気速度(TAS)と対地速度(GS)の差分が、そのままβ項の推定値となる。これは他産業にはない航空データ特有の性質であり、外生的な気象予報に頼ることなく、実フライトデータそのものから計量を学習できる。 GI理論の三条件(命題1.1)を航空データで充足するための工夫 GI Vol.1 命題1.1は、VAE(変分自己符号化器)から可微分多様体を構築するために以下の三条件を要求する。 条件(i):VAEデコーダのC³級滑らかさ 活性化関数の選択が鍵となる。航空多様体では高度・速度・位置の急激な変化を扱うため、ReLU(折れ曲がり点で1階微分が不連続)は使用できない。全層にtanh(双曲線正接関数、C∞級)を使用することで、測地線方程式が要求するクリストッフェル記号の計算に必要な2階微分の連続性を保証した。 条件(ii):ヤコビ行列のフルランク VAE訓練後にデコーダのヤコビ行列のSVD(特異値分解)を実施し、最小特異値0.312(ゼロから十分離れている)を確認した。また、KNN(k近傍)保存率0.891(目標値0.85以上)により、潜在空間の幾何学が実フライトデータの多様体構造を忠実に反映していることを検証した。 条件(iii):ランダー条件 ‖β‖_α < 1 この条件は「風速が航空機の真対気速度を超えない」という物理的条件と等価である。787-9のTAS(約250 m/s、マッハ0.85)に対し、北太平洋のジェット気流は典型的に50〜100 m/s(最大値で約0.40の比率)であり、条件は全区間で満たされた。実測値は出発時0.38、飛行中最大0.56であった。なお、0.65を超えると時変フィンスラー計量の理論的安定性が保証されなくなることから、超過時にはリーマン計量へのフォールバックを設計段階から組み込んだ。この「理論の限界を正直に設計する」姿勢は、航空安全(DO-178C)との整合性の観点からも不可欠である。 このほか、GFS・ECMWFの気象予報モデルとADS-Bの実測値を統合した二重データソース構造により、β項の推定誤差を±0.04以内に抑え、通信途絶時でも機上Embodied Agentが最後の既知計量から局所的に更新を継続できるアーキテクチャを採用した。 本書の読者へのメッセージ 本書が描く世界では、一人のエンジニア(カイト)が「今まで数学と物理とプログラミングだけ学んできた。でも今回の一件に参加してから、国際政治と法律を本腰入れて学ばなきゃと思っている」と語る場面がある。これは、GI理論の実践者に求められる知識の横断性を象徴している。 航空運航にGI理論を適用するためには、以下が同時に必要である。 数学の知識——フィンスラー幾何学(ランダー計量・チャーン接続・測地線方程式)、位相幾何学(コホモロジー群、ジグザグ・パーシステンス)、最適制御理論(ポントリャーギンの最大原理・随伴変数)、情報幾何学(フィッシャー情報量計量・VAE引き戻し計量)が、互いに接続した一つの体系として使いこなせること。本書に登場する数学は、それぞれ独立した分野として一流大学の大学院レベルで教えられているが、それらを横断するカリキュラムは2026年現在、世界のどこにも存在しない。 コード実装とAIアルゴリズムの知見——VAEの訓練ループとC³条件を満たすアーキテクチャ設計、フィンスラー測地線の数値解法(約40秒で再計算できる実装)、14体のAI Agentの並列設計と通信プロトコル、形式検証ツール(Lean 4)とZKML(ゼロ知識証明による機械学習の計算検証)の組み合わせ。理論を「動く実装」に落とし込む工学的知見が不可欠である。 地政学と国際法の知識——シカゴ条約の条文、二国間航空協定の枠組み、非国家主体が生み出す法の外側のリスク、制裁リスト(OFAC・EU・国連)のリアルタイム監視。数学が設計した航路が「法的に飛べるか」を判断するためには、これらを数式と同じ精度で理解する必要がある。数学が地形を設計し、法律と国際政治がその地形の制約を決める。 判断力と勇気——本書の核心的な問いは「測地線を信じますか」という一言に集約される。数学的に最適な経路が存在すると証明されても、通信が途絶した北極海上空でロシア領空の12海里以内まで接近するか否かの最終判断は、機長が下す。AIは測地線を計算し、人間が決断する。理論の限界を正直に認識した上で、不完全な情報のもとで行動する意志——これが、GI理論の実践者に求められる最後の、そして最も重要な条件である。 GI理論は「一人の天才が全部わかる」ことを前提としない。数学者・エンジニア・パイロット・ディスパッチャー・アクチュアリー・地政学アナリストが、同じ数学的言語で対話できるチームを前提としている。本書は、そのチームがどのように機能するかの具体的な描写でもある。 なぜ航空業界にはGIを用いた統合リスク管理が不可欠なのか 航空業界が直面するリスクは、他産業と比較して以下の三点で構造的に異なる。 第一に、リスクの同時多発性と相互依存性。本書が描くように、気象リスク(ジェット気流の予報外れ)・運航安全リスク(ETOPSの制約)・地政学的リスク(FIRの閉鎖)・保険リスク(戦争リスク条項)・通信リスク(太陽フレアによる電離層障害)が12時間のフライト中に同時に発生し、かつ相互に依存する。ETOPS代替空港の気象悪化が保険ファイバーのH¹を変化させ、それがルート変更の可否に影響する。これらを個別に管理するサイロ型リスク管理は、構造的に破綻する。 第二に、リアルタイム性の要求。航空機は時速900 km で飛行している。地政学的な情勢変化(NOTAMによる空域制限の発出)から気象の急変まで、判断のサイクルタイムは分単位である。経営会議で半期に一度リスクを審議するような産業とは根本的に異なる。GI理論が採用する「測地線のリアルタイム再計算(約40秒)と14体のAI Agentによる並列監視」は、この要求に対応する設計である。 第三に、「通常の経路が存在しない」状況への対応。従来の航路最適化は「既存の航空路の中からどれを選ぶか」という選択問題を前提としてきた。しかし、地政学的緊張が高まり複数の大国が同時期に領空を閉鎖する現代では、既存のどの航空路も選択できない状況——本書でいうH¹(B, F) ≠ 0の状態——が現実のシナリオとして生じうる。この場合に必要なのは「新しい測地線を設計する数学」であり、従来のグリッド探索アルゴリズムでは対応できない。ランダー計量上の連続的な測地線方程式を解く能力は、まさにこの「通常の経路が存在しない」局面のためにある。 さらに、航空業界は乗客の生命安全という最高度の責任を負う。DO-178C(航空電子機器ソフトウェア安全基準)との整合、ETOPS認証要件、各国航空当局への説明責任——これらを充足しながらAIシステムを運航に組み込む際には、「数学的に正しいことと、航空安全として正しいことは別の概念」(本書第15章、CTO ヨルゲンの言葉)という緊張を常に意識する必要がある。ZKMLによる計算の形式検証と、パイロットの最終判断権限の明示的な保持が、この緊張を解消する設計原則となる。 GI Ver.3への展望 本書(GIケーススタディ第11作、航空産業編)は、GI Vol.3の数学的素材を先取りする形で設計されている。 GI Vol.1(リーマン計量・フィンスラー計量・H¹コホモロジー・VAE引き戻し計量)とGI Vol.2(シンプレクティック幾何・ワイル幾何・ジグザグ・パーシステンス・AI Agent設計)で確立した枠組みを、本書は航空という極限状況のもとで実証した。北太平洋でのリアルタイムβ項更新、北極海での通信途絶時11分間の自律運用、二つのコホモロジー問題の同時発生(ETOPS穴と保険穴)、極渦による計量急変時のリーマンへのフォールバックと時変フィンスラー計量の未解決問題——これらは、GI Vol.3が扱うべき数学的課題を実データから照射している。 GI Vol.3では次の数学領域の統合を予定している:シンプレクティック積分法の長期安定シミュレーションへの応用(エネルギー保存と構造保存)、ワイル幾何のゲージ不変性をAI出力検証に適用するフレームワーク、情報幾何学(フィッシャー情報量計量)によるSIGINT異常検知との接続、最適輸送理論(ワッサースタイン計量)による確率分布の時間変化追跡、双曲幾何(ポアンカレ埋め込み)による組織・ネットワーク構造の表現。 本書の後日談(第16章)では、天翔航空の航空多様体と曙海運の海上多様体の統合構想——海と空が同じ数学的言語で動く日本発の地理情報多様体インフラ——が語られる。これがGIケーススタディ第12作(海運産業編)へと引き継がれ、GI Vol.3の理論的裏付けとなる予定である。 GI理論が目指すのは「数学と、法律と、地政学と、工学が交差する場所に立てる人間が設計するシステム」である。その交差点は、2026年現在、世界のどの大学のカリキュラムにも存在しない。本ケーススタディシリーズが、その交差点を実践の場から構築するための素材となることを期待する。

title: Headlines You Won't Forget: Can Pronoun Insertion Increase Memorability?
abstract: For unrestricted data access, please go to the newest version of this dataset. This is the data repository for the CMCL 2026 paper "Headlines You Won't Forget: Can Pronoun Insertion Increase Memorability?" The zip-file "LLM revisions and Annotations" contains three files: annotation_samples.json and annotation_samples_2.json contain all LLM-revisions.annotations_of_LLM_revisions.json contains the non-aggregated annotation data for all LLM-revisions. Annotations for accuracy_subclass are ordered as follows: [misrepresentation, omission, addition]. Annotations for style subclass are ordered as [grammar, awkward style, inconsistent]. In the zip-file "Memory Experiment Data", we provide non-aggregated results of the memory experiment (experiment_data.json), as well as the recalled items matched to their respective headline id's (headline_items_matched). headlines.json provides information about the revision type, and group assignment of headline items. We further provide aggregated results in csv-files. Files for each study are provided in separate sub-directories. If you use this dataset in your research please cite the paper.

title: Pretrained Models and Reproducibility Archive for "From Characters to Syntax: Characterizing the Accuracy–Robustness Trade-off in Cross-Domain Authorship Verification"
abstract: This repository contains the pretrained model weights, vectorizer pipelines, and ablation study checkpoints for the paper "From Characters to Syntax: Characterizing the Accuracy–Robustness Trade-off in Cross-Domain Authorship Verification". The provided models were trained and evaluated across three distinct text domains (fanfiction, personal blogs, and corporate emails) to investigate the fundamental vulnerability of stylometric systems against semantic-preserving paraphrase attacks. Contents of this archive: Robust Siamese: The best-performing cross-domain model utilizing character n-gram features (includes .pth weights, vectorizer.pkl , and scaler.pkl ). Cross-Domain (CD) Siamese: The baseline generalist character 4-gram model trained across all domains. Robust DANN (Domain-Adversarial Neural Network): The multi-view syntactic feature model trained for high adversarial robustness. BERT Baseline: The contextual baseline model used for comparative evaluation. Syntactic Ablation Models: Pretrained checkpoints isolating Part-of-Speech (POS) trigrams, function word frequencies, and readability metrics to demonstrate the specific drivers of robustness in stylometric features. Usage: These weights are intended to be used directly with the PyTorch and Scikit-Learn inference pipelines provided in the official GitHub repository. Researchers can utilize this archive to perfectly reproduce the cross-domain accuracy (up to 86.2%) and attack success rate evaluations presented in the manuscript.

title: VentGuard: A Machine Learning-Based Real-Time Anomaly Detection and Early Warning System for Mechanical Ventilator Monitoring
abstract: Mechanical ventilation is a critical life-support intervention for patients with respiratory failure in intensive care units. However, timely detection of ventilator-related anomalies remains challenging due to the complexity of respiratory data streams. This paper presents VentGuard, a web-based platform that combines real-time data visualization with machine learning algorithms for automated anomaly detection in mechanical ventilator monitoring. Our system implements six unsupervised learning algorithms including Isolation Forest, One-Class SVM, and DBSCAN, enabling comparative analysis and flexible model deployment. We propose a ML-enhanced detection approach that augments traditional rule-based clinical thresholds with machine learning pattern recognition. Experimental evaluation on 8,115 real-world ventilator records demonstrates that ML enhancement achieves 78-89% anomaly detection rates, providing consistent improvements of 3-10 percentage points over rule-based baseline methods, with Isolation Forest and One-Class SVM showing the most stable performance across varying training data volumes. The system’s modular architecture supports configurable training and real-time alert generation, making it suitable for deployment in critical care environments.

title: Design of Robotic Arm Control System Based on Fuzzy PID Algorithm
abstract: Addressing the nonlinear and strongly coupled characteristics of robotic manipulators, along with the poor robustness and limited adaptability of traditional PID control under complex operating conditions, this paper presents the designed of a robotic arm control system based on a fuzzy PID algorithm. Initially, the hardware of the robotic arm was divided into four core modules, clarifying the structure and collaborative logic of each component. Subsequently, a fuzzy PID controller is constructed, employing a six-step core process to achieve dynamic tuning of PID parameters. Finally, a simulation model of a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) with load disturbance rejection is built using Matlab/Simulink to compare the control performance of traditional PID and fuzzy PID. The simulation results demonstrate that the fuzzy PID algorithm can reduce the three-phase current imbalance of the motor from 8.3% to 3.1%, significantly suppress torque and speed overshoot, substantially shorten disturbance recovery time, and limit steadystate fluctuations of the system to only$\mathbf{2 0 \%} \boldsymbol{\sim} \mathbf{2 5 \%}$of those observed with traditional PID. This algorithm effectively enhances the dynamic response speed and disturbance rejection capability of the robotic arm drive system, overcoming the limitations of traditional PID in nonlinear systems and providing a viable solution for optimizing control algorithms for robotic arms in high-end intelligent equipment.

title: LMDA: Lightweight Multiauthority CP-ABE Scheme Based on Dynamic Attributes for System Wide Information Management
abstract: The System Wide Information Management (SWIM) system serves as an advanced platform for managing and sharing diverse aviation data, such as aeronautical, flight, and meteorological information. With the exponential growth of aviation data, ensuring data security and privacy within SWIM has become increasingly important. Ciphertext-Policy Attribute-Based Encryption (CP-ABE) is widely regarded as an effective cryptographic technique for ensuring secure and private data access. However, traditional CP-ABE schemes rely on computationally expensive bilinear pairings, which are unsuitable for resource-constrained aviation Internet of Things application scenarios in SWIM, such as Aircraft Access to SWIM. To address this limitation, we propose a lightweight multi-authority CP-ABE scheme based on dynamic attributes. This scheme replaces bilinear pairing operations with efficient scalar multiplication on elliptic curve points and outsources most decryption operations to outsourcing decryption nodes, thereby significantly reducing computational overhead. In addition, this scheme introduces a dynamic attribute mechanism to support fine-grained access control, and outsources data verification and attribute revocation to the blockchain to ensure data integrity. Security analysis shows that our scheme achieves indistinguishability under adaptive chosen-ciphertext attacks and is resistant to collusion attacks. Experimental evaluations further demonstrate that our scheme significantly enhances computational and communication efficiency.

title: Reversible Quantum Digital Circuits and Quantum Random Number Generation Using Qiskit
abstract: Quantum computing requires logic operations to be implemented as reversible transformations. Classical combinational circuits must therefore be redesigned using reversible gate structures when mapped to quantum systems. In this work, fundamental quantum digital circuits are implemented using CNOT and Toffoli gates using the Qiskit framework.In addition, an 8-qubit Quantum Random Number Generator (QRNG) is developed and analyzed. Hadamard operations are applied to an 8-qubit register to produce a uniform superposition over 256 states. Measurement in the computational basis generates an 8-bit result per execution. By repeating the circuit 16 independent times and concatenation of the outputs produce a 128-bit random sequence. The QRNG is evaluated using Dirac notation, density operator representation and entropy analysis to verify uniform probability distribution under ideal simulation conditions.Simulation results confirm the correct logical functionality of the reversible arithmetic circuits and demonstrate high entropy random sequence generation using quantum measurement. The presented framework provides a structured approach for implementing digital logic and randomness generation in Qiskit.

title: Mastering AI Communication: The Art of Prompt Engineering
abstract: This chapter explains the four ingredients of a perfect prompt: be specific, give context, set boundaries, and choose the flavor. Common mistakes that kill the prompts include the “throw everything at the wall” approach; the “figure it out yourself” problem; and the “one size fits all” trap. Most clients actually appreciate the efficiency, as long as they are adding their own expertise and personal touch. The magic happens when they combine that efficiency with the skills, creativity, and understanding of what the clients actually need. When it comes to fact-checking with artificial intelligence (AI), one can use a few key strategies to ensure accuracy. For data, research, or client-facing reports that require complete accuracy, always supplement AI fact-check with a quick Google search or a trusted database. Prompt engineering is not about coding; it is about conversation.

title: Do Hallucination Neurons Generalize? Evidence from Cross-Domain Transfer in LLMs
abstract: Recent work identifies a sparse set of "hallucination neurons" (H-neurons), less than 0.1% of feed-forward network neurons, that reliably predict when large language models will hallucinate. These neurons are identified on general-knowledge question answering and shown to generalize to new evaluation instances. We ask a natural follow-up question: do H-neurons generalize across knowledge domains? Using a systematic cross-domain transfer protocol across 6 domains (general QA, legal, financial, science, moral reasoning, and code vulnerability) and 5 open-weight models (3B to 8B parameters), we find they do not. Classifiers trained on one domain's H-neurons achieve AUROC 0.783 within-domain but only 0.563 when transferred to a different domain (delta = 0.220, p < 0.001), a degradation consistent across all models tested. Our results suggest that hallucination is not a single mechanism with a universal neural signature, but rather involves domain-specific neuron populations that differ depending on the knowledge type being queried. This finding has direct implications for the deployment of neuron-level hallucination detectors, which must be calibrated per domain rather than trained once and applied universally.

title: Low-energy spectrum of double-junction superconducting circuits in the Born-Oppenheimer approximation
abstract: The superconductor-insulator-superconductor Josephson junction is the fundamental nonlinear element of superconducting circuits. Connecting two junctions in series gives rise to higher-harmonic content in the total energy-phase relation, enabling new design opportunities in multimode circuits. However, the double-junction element hosts an internal mode whose spectrum is set by the finite capacitances of the individual junctions. Using a Born-Oppenheimer approximation that treats the additional mode as fast compared to the qubit mode, we analyze the double-junction circuit element shunted by a large capacitor. Here, we derive an effective single-mode model of the qubit containing a correction term owing to the presence of the internal mode. In experimentally relevant parameter regimes, we numerically find that our model accurately describes the low-energy spectrum of the qubit. We further discuss how eliminating the internal degree of freedom affects the system's periodic boundary conditions and leads to non-uniqueness in performing the Born-Oppenheimer approximation. Finally, we analyze the harmonic content of the double-junction element and discuss its sensitivity to charge noise.

title: Hermes Seal: Zero-Knowledge Assurance for Autonomous Vehicle Communications
abstract: The application of zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs) in autonomous systems is an emerging area of research, motivated by the growing need for regulatory compliance, transparent auditing, and trustworthy operation in decentralized environments. zk-SNARK is a powerful cryptographic tool that allows a party (the prover) to prove to another party (the verifier) that a statement about its own internal state is true, without revealing sensitive or proprietary data about that state. This paper proposes Hermes Seal: a zk-SNARK-based ZKP framework for enabling privacy-preserving, verifiable communication in vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) and vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) networks. The framework allows autonomous systems to generate cryptographic proofs of perception and decision-related computations without revealing proprietary models, sensor data, or internal system states, thereby supporting interoperability across heterogeneous autonomous systems. We present two real-world case studies implemented and empirically evaluated within our framework, demonstrating a step toward verifiable autonomous system information exchanges. The first demonstrates real-time proof generation and verification, achieving 8 ms proof generation and 1 ms verification on a GPU, while the second evaluates the performance of an autonomous vehicle perception stack, enabling proof of computation without exposing proprietary or confidential data. Furthermore, the framework can be integrated into AV perception stacks to facilitate verifiable interoperability and privacy-preserving cooperative perception. The demonstration code for this project is open source, available on Github.

title: Hidden-Test Distribution Science (HTDS): Core Field Specification, Staged Development Ladder, and Minimal Executable Kernel
abstract: Summary: HTDS Core Set v1.0 formalizes Hidden-Test Distribution Science as a lawful field for decision-making under hidden-test uncertainty. Rather than treating the hidden test as a secret answer key to be guessed, HTDS models a feasible family of hidden worlds constrained by public shadows, compresses those worlds by score-relevant equivalence, updates beliefs over them lawfully, and selects robust controllers under uncertainty. The archive introduces the core ontology of the field, including hidden-world families, public shadows, regime catalogs, controllers, equivalence classes, posterior world families, diversity measured through failure covariance, replayable receipts, and unresolved uncertainty scars. It includes the canonical core specifications, the staged development ladder from early hardened formulations through protocol, factorization, freeze, and runtime layers, and a minimal executable kernel that demonstrates the science in runnable form. HTDS is presented not as a leakage doctrine or leaderboard superstition, but as a scientific framework for lawful hidden-world inference, robust controller selection, and memory-bound freeze under partial observability. Keywords: Hidden-Test Distribution Science, HTDS, hidden-world inference, public shadows, score-relevant equivalence, controller robustness, partial observability, posterior world families, regime catalogs, failure covariance, lawful leaderboard inference, replayable freeze, uncertainty scars, executable scientific governance

title: Apparent Local Robustness Under Context-Reduced Interfaces: A Minimal Synthetic Stress Test
abstract: This technical note presents a minimal synthetic stress test on local robustness under reduced context interfaces in large language model inference. A controlled dataset of 100 multiple-choice instances is introduced across four evidence regimes: easy local retrieval, distributed evidence integration, conflict-sensitive update resolution, and position-sensitive retrieval. The same model is evaluated under three interfaces: FULL, RECENT, and a deterministic COMPRESSED interface retaining only the first sentence of each block. The main result is a clear regime-dependent dissociation: perfect local robustness is preserved in the easy regime, while strong interface-specific failures emerge outside it. The note is strictly diagnostic and local in scope, and argues that local benchmark robustness under a reduced context interface does not imply global behavioral equivalence across evidence regimes.

title: Logic of ER I - Core Logic & Meta-Theory: A Conservative Predicate Extension of First-Order Linear Tense Logic
abstract: Existential Realism (ER) proposes a two-tier ontology: only the present exists, yet the past and the future are real. This thesis arises from the diagnosis that in debates on the ontology of time, “existence” and “reality” are often implicitly identified, thereby making presentism and eternalism appear as competing positions that merely disagree about the extension of a single ontological predicate. ER instead separates a narrow, present-bound predicate of existence from a broader notion of reality that allows non-present entities to count as real when, for instance, they existed in the past or will exist in the future, allowing these to participate in time-directed deductions. This paper develops the core system ERL (Existential-Realism Logic): a classical first-order linear temporal logic, in the Prior tradition, enriched with two distinguished unary predicates E (“exists now”) and R (“is real”). ERL is (i) syntactically defined with precision, (ii) given a model-theoretic semantics via Kripke-style ER-frames, (iii) axiomatized through a Hilbert-style system, and (iv) supported by metalogical results establishing soundness and outlining a canonical completeness program. Where strong completeness requires additional standard assumptions (such as Henkinization or generalized models), this is made explicit. Further central technical results include: conservativity over classical first-order linear temporal logic without E/R; an explicit Barcan profile (Barcan schemas hold for unrestricted quantifiers under constant domains, but may fail for existence-restricted quantifiers ∀ᴱ/∃ᴱ); and non-reducibility results (E is not definable, over the class of ER-models, using purely temporal operators; R cannot be forced as a definitional derivative of E together with temporal operators). The overall aim is to demonstrate that ER constitutes a logically stable and metalogically respectable position within established modal-temporal traditions, without unnecessarily over-engineering the formal system. Soundness is proven; completeness is outlined via a canonical-model strategy but left for full technical development in subsequent work.

title: Empowering Bengali Language in Drone Control with Artificial Neural Networks
abstract: With drone technology advancing, there’s a growing need for intuitive control methods. Traditionally, drones rely on remote controllers, demanding trained operators for piloting. This paper introduces a novel approach to drone control using Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) and Bengali voice commands, aiming to simplify drone piloting for users without prior experience with remote controllers. A dataset of 6010 Bengali audio samples, comprising 15 distinct voice commands, was meticulously curated to reflect diverse environmental and speaker variations. Leveraging Mel-frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs), an ANN-based model interprets Bengali voice commands to control drone movements in real-world scenarios. Commands like “Take Off/BNN ”, “Turn Right/BNN”, “Go Up/BNN”, “Move Forward/BNN”, “Stop/BNN” are among those utilized for model training. A system architecture centered around a Raspberry Pi facilitates the integration of the trained model, ensuring seamless drone operation during flight. Through extensive experimentation, an impressive accuracy rate of 73% was achieved, underscoring the model’s robustness in command classification.

title: A Deep Learning-Based Multi-Modal Collaborative Intervention Model for Adolescent Physical and Mental Health Optimization
abstract: Adolescent physical and mental health is the cornerstone of national human capital development, with sports interventions playing a pivotal role in boosting adolescents’ physical and psychological well-being and artificial intelligence offering critical support for the digital and precision transformation of such interventions, yet their practical implementation is confronted with multiple interwoven challenges. This study adopts literature review, logical analysis, questionnaire surveys and mathematical statistics as research methods, and conducts empirical research on 201 adolescents aged 12-18 from three pilot smart sports schools, which objectively identifies five major practical challenges including inadequate data monitoring systems, ambiguous ethical boundaries, prominent data security risks, suboptimal intervention efficacy and limited adolescent AI awareness. On this basis, the study constructs a human-centered, collaborative, precise and safe multidimensional collaborative intervention model with a four-tier technical architecture that forms a complete intelligent closed loop, and this human-centered and collaborative model uniquely anchors adolescents’ bodily autonomy and multi-stakeholder synergy at its core, marking a key innovative breakthrough in integrating AI technology with adolescent sports health intervention in a people-oriented way. The study also proposes targeted optimization pathways in five dimensions to systematically address the above challenges. The research findings provide important theoretical and practical references for deepening the integration of artificial intelligence technologies and advancing the intelligent governance of adolescent physical and mental health.

title: A Multi-Modal Intelligent Learning System for Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Prediction Using Advanced Neural Optimization Techniques
abstract: ALS is a terminal neurodegenerative disease that results in progressive degeneration of motor neurons and respiratory failure that has a significant effect on the survival of patients. The symptoms of ALS should be identified early so as to intervene effectively. This paper will suggest a multimodal smart learning model to predict ALS based on the MIMIC-III clinical data. The system combines clinical, physiological and time-series data with a hybrid CNN-LSTM structure in order to capture spatial and temporal patterns. Particle Swarm Optimization and Genetic Algorithms are used to optimize hyperparameters and feature selection to increase the model performance. It was experimentally shown that the proposed GA-PSO optimized CNN-LSTM model has an accuracy of 95, and a high precision, recall and F1-score. The reliability and robustness of the model is also proved through confusion matrix and ROC analysis. The research identifies the usefulness of the multi-modal data integration and neural optimization in the prediction of ALS, and provides an opportunity to create an intelligent clinical decision support framework.

title: A Metaheuristic Framework for Minimizing Design Errors in Low-Pass Chebyshev Filter Synthesis
abstract: This paper presents the Chaotic Oppositional Bald Eagle Search (COBES) algorithm, a refined version of the Bald Eagle Search (BES) method. The proposed technique optimizes the design errors in fractional-order low-pass Chebyshev filters (FOLPCF). The proposed method incorporates oppositional learning for improved initialization of population and logistic chaotic mapping to enhance the balance between exploration and exploitation phases. COBES is used to determine optimal transfer function coefficients for third- and fifth-order FOLPCFs and stability is assured using Jury-Marden constraints. COBES surpasses PSO, FA, and RGA in terms of error minimization (MSE−4. The results prove COBES as an efficient optimizer for the design of digital fractional-order filter.

title: Importance of Electronic Entropy for Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
abstract: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) enable large-scale atomistic simulations but remain challenged in describing mixed-valence materials where charge ordering strongly influences thermodynamic stability. Here we investigate the role of electronic entropy in MLIP structural optimization of the battery cathode material NaFePO4. We show that conventional MLIPs fail to reproduce the correct stability of intermediate Na concentrations because structural optimization leads to incorrect Fe^{2+}/Fe^{3+} charge assignments, resulting in erroneous energy ordering and convex-hull predictions. Analysis of magnetic moments during structural optimization reveals that MLIPs are unable to capture electronic entropy associated with charge ordering. To address this limitation, we introduce an approach that embeds charge-state information directly into the MLIP representation by distinguishing between Fe^{2+} and Fe^{3+} environments during training. Retraining CHGNet, cPaiNN, and MACE with this representation enables accurate structural optimization, correct identification of charge ordering, and improved agreement with density functional theory convex hulls. Our results demonstrate that incorporating electronic entropy into MLIP representations is essential for modeling charge-disordered materials and provide a practical framework for extending MLIP simulations to mixed-valence transition-metal systems.

title: Machine Learning-Based Methods for Engineering System Optimization
abstract: Optimization problems are at the core of many engineering systems, where performance, efficiency, and reliability must be improved under practical constraints. Existing studies on machine learning based optimization often emphasize algorithmic development, while providing limited discussion on how learning models support decision making under real engineering constraints. In recent years, machine learning has become an increasingly important tool for addressing optimization tasks that are difficult to solve using conventional analytical or heuristic approaches. Instead of relying on explicit system models, machine learning methods enable optimization strategies to be learned directly from data. This paper presents an overview of machine learning based methods for engineering system optimization. The discussion focuses on commonly used learning models, their roles in optimization workflows, and their application in representative engineering domains. In addition, practical challenges related to interpretability, data dependence, computational burden, and engineering deployment are examined. The aim of this review is to provide engineers and researchers with a clear understanding of how machine learning is currently used for optimization and what limitations must be considered in real engineering practice.

title: AI as Mirrors: How Interaction Shapes the AI Experience
abstract: Conversational AI systems are often described as having distinct personalities or styles. This paper argues that these perceived differences are not primarily properties of the models themselves, but emerge from the interaction between user behavior and system design. AI systems function as reflective environments that take in user signals and return them in structured and often amplified form. Through repeated interaction, this creates the appearance of stable personality. What users call “AI personality” is not a fixed trait, but the interaction reflected back. Understanding AI as a shaped interaction system clarifies how behavior emerges, why experiences differ across users, and how responsibility is shared between user input and system design.

title: THE EXPERT SYSTEM OF THE OIL RIG DRILLING WINCH
abstract: Topicality. The increasing complexity of oil rig drilling operations requires reliable and intelligent tools for timely detection and elimination of equipment failures. Winch brake malfunctions pose a significant risk to operational safety, making the development of automated diagnostic systems a critical task. The subject of the research is models, methods and tools for building an expert system for automated diagnostics of faults in winch brakes of drilling rigs on oil platforms, as well as the processes of detection, interpretation and support for making corrective decisions in real time. The purpose of this article is to develop a knowledge-based expert system capable of detecting winch brake disorders in oil rig drilling operations and supporting automated corrective decision-making. The proposed system is based on a rule-based knowledge representation using IF and THEN inference mechanisms and heuristic frames that integrate technological parameters and their dynamic changes. Artificial intelligence techniques are applied to enable adaptive learning from previously encountered operational scenarios and to update the knowledge base. The following results were obtained. A knowledge-based expert system for oil rig drilling winch diagnostics was developed. The system successfully identifies potential brake failures and recommends corrective actions based on expert-defined rules. Experimental evaluation demonstrates improved accuracy and efficiency in fault detection and decision support. Conclusion. The developed expert system ensures effective detection of winch brake disorders, enhances operational efficiency, and increases the reliability and safety of oil rig drilling equipment.

title: An AI-powered Tamil Voice Assistant for Farmers to Access Agricultural Schemes and Support
abstract: Despite Tamil Nadu’s enormous progress in e- governance, rural farmers find it hard to use the state’s agri- culture welfare schemes because of low digital literacy skills, language barriers, and complex application processes. To address this problem, creating a voice-based assistant powered by AI (and built for Tamil) enables farmers to communicate with government resources through spoken Tamil. Using ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition) for speech-to-text conversion, Natural Language Understanding (NLU) for intent and entity extraction, a rule- based eligibility engine for personalized scheme recommendation, OCR (Optical Character Recognition) for document processing, and TTS (Text-to-Speech) for audio outputs, the proposed system provides users with a complete conversational system that allows them to search for schemes, determine eligibility for schemes, and submit their applications. The system’s hardware and software show very promising results: the ASR system produced a Word Error Rate (WER) of 0.0833, which indicates that it accurately recognized speech with good accuracy; and the NLU produced an F1 score of 0.986 from its interaction with the hardware, indicating accurate understanding of user intent and successful extraction of relevant information from users. Therefore, the design of this system, combined with its functionality, greatly reduces reliance on intermediaries and increases the access of rural farmers to agricultural welfare schemes, thereby enabling provision of these services to residents in a manner that is both fully inclusive, and has significantly simplified the provision of access to these services.

title: Automatic Generation of a Mechanical Properties Question-Answering Data Set for Language Model Benchmarking: A Comparative Study of BERT, XLNet, and LLaMA Models
abstract: Contextualized language models offer new opportunities for mining materials-science information from literature, but progress is limited by the absence of domain-specific question-answering (QA) data sets. This study addresses this by introducing MechQA, a data set of 202,068 pairs of questions and answers about mechanical properties that have been automatically distilled from 125,967 articles in the literature. Unlike small manually curated QA benchmarks or approaches that rely on domain-specific pretraining, MechQA provides a large-scale, automatically generated training resource derived directly from the primary literature. It covers five fundamental mechanical properties of materials: ultimate tensile strength, yield strength, fracture strength, Young's modulus, and ductility. Manual evaluation of this data set confirmed its high quality (precision 83.76%, recall 89.09%, F1 score 86.34%). We apply MechQA to fine-tune three representative transformer models: two extractive models, BERT-base and XLNet-base, each with 110 M parameters, and a generative LLaMA-3.1-Instruct model with 8B parameters fine-tuned using low-rank adaptation (LoRA). The MechQA data set was partitioned into 181,722 training and 20,346 validation QA pairs for this application. On the validation set, domain-specific extractive models achieve strong Exact Match (EM) and F1 score performance (BERT: 78.03% EM/84.50% F1; XLNet: 78.21% EM/84.70% F1) with improved expected calibration error (ECE) of 7.98% and 6.25%, respectively, while the LLaMA-domain model achieves 80.48% EM/86.25% F1 with an ECE of 8.08%. Notably, the two extractive models exhibit competitive performance despite their significantly smaller parameter size compared to the LLaMA model. These results demonstrate that automatic QA data set generation, coupled with targeted fine-tuning, provides an effective data-centric method for domain adaptation of language models for materials science.

title: A Hierarchical Gaussian Process Approach to Understanding Mental Health Trajectories via Item Response Theory Models
abstract: Longitudinal mental health assessments in mobile health (mHealth) settings are useful for monitoring subjects' mental health statuses but are often difficult to analyze because they generally appear on an ordinal scale and at unequal time intervals. In this article, we explore the use of Gaussian processes (GPs) and hierarchical modeling techniques to understand mental health trajectories based on repeated multi-item mHealth surveys on a Likert scale. We introduce the GP model for health trajectories, which is based on item response theory. In the study of trajectories, a subject's longitudinal collection of mHealth responses can be thought of as a single high-dimensional observation. We show how the GP is flexible enough to capture trends in individual trajectories even with the challenges associated with high-dimensional data. We also demonstrate how basis splines can be used to effectively capture nonlinear trends in the mean function of the GP. The high-dimension and ordinal nature of the data often make sampling from the posterior distribution in a Bayesian setting too slow to be practical. We show that using a Hilbert approximation for the GP trajectories can facilitate efficient sampling. We apply these methods to a longitudinal study that monitored college students' self-esteem.

title: ClimateCheck 2026: Scientific Fact-Checking and Disinformation Narrative Classification of Climate-related Claims
abstract: Automatically verifying climate-related claims against scientific literature is a challenging task, complicated by the specialised nature of scholarly evidence and the diversity of rhetorical strategies underlying climate disinformation. ClimateCheck 2026 is the second iteration of a shared task addressing this challenge, expanding on the 2025 edition with tripled training data and a new disinformation narrative classification task. Running from January to February 2026 on the CodaBench platform, the competition attracted 20 registered participants and 8 leaderboard submissions, with systems combining dense retrieval pipelines, cross-encoder ensembles, and large language models with structured hierarchical reasoning. In addition to standard evaluation metrics (Recall@K and Binary Preference), we adapt an automated framework to assess retrieval quality under incomplete annotations, exposing systematic biases in how conventional metrics rank systems. A cross-task analysis further reveals that not all climate disinformation is equally verifiable, potentially implicating how future fact-checking systems should be designed.

title: Geometrical Constructions of Purity Testing Protocols and Their Applications to Quantum Communication
abstract: Purity testing protocols (PTPs), also known as Bell state testing protocols, i.e., protocols that decide with high probability whether or not a distributed bipartite quantum state is a tensor product of Bell states, have been proven to be a useful tool in many quantum communication applications. In this paper, we provide geometrical constructions for such protocols that originate directly from classical linear error correcting codes (LECCs), in a way that the properties of the resulting PTP are completely determined from those of the LECC used in the construction. We investigate the implications of our results in various quantum communication tasks, including error detection, entanglement purification for general quantum error models and quantum message authentication.

title: EngineAD: A Real-World Vehicle Engine Anomaly Detection Dataset
abstract: The progress of Anomaly Detection (AD) in safety-critical domains, such as transportation, is severely constrained by the lack of large-scale, real-world benchmarks. To address this, we introduce EngineAD, a novel, multivariate dataset comprising high-resolution sensor telemetry collected from a fleet of 25 commercial vehicles over a six-month period. Unlike synthetic datasets, EngineAD features authentic operational data labeled with expert annotations, distinguishing normal states from subtle indicators of incipient engine faults. We preprocess the data into 300-timestep segments of 8 principal components and establish an initial benchmark using nine diverse one-class anomaly detection models. Our experiments reveal significant performance variability across the vehicle fleet, underscoring the challenge of cross-vehicle generalization. Furthermore, our findings corroborate recent literature, showing that simple classical methods (e.g., K-Means and One-Class SVM) are often highly competitive with, or superior to, deep learning approaches in this segment-based evaluation. By publicly releasing EngineAD, we aim to provide a realistic, challenging resource for developing robust and field-deployable anomaly detection and anomaly prediction solutions for the automotive industry. title: Agentic Commerce Applications: How Autonomous AI Is Redefining the Retail & E-Commerce Industry
abstract: Retail and e-commerce have steadily evolved from manual operations and rule-based automation to data-driven analytics and, more recently, generative AI systems that assist human decision-making. The next inflection point in this trajectory is agentic artificial intelligence—systems that can interpret goals, plan multi-step actions, coordinate with other agents, and autonomously execute commercial workflows within defined constraints. This paper introduces the concept of agentic commerce, where autonomous AI agents move beyond recommendation and insight generation to actively manage end-to-end retail processes across customer experience, merchandising, operations, and governance.Drawing on recent advances in large language models, multimodal reasoning, and enterprise AI architectures, the paper synthesizes academic literature and industry practices to propose a structured framework for deploying agentic systems in modern retail ecosystems. We examine how agentic capabilities enable continuous demand sensing, dynamic assortment and pricing decisions, conversational and anticipatory shopping experiences, and real-time operational orchestration across omnichannel environments. Beyond technical architecture, the paper addresses organizational, ethical, and governance considerations required to safely operationalize autonomy at scale.By distinguishing assistive AI from truly agentic systems and outlining progressive levels of autonomy in retail decision-making, this work provides both researchers and practitioners with a foundation for understanding how autonomous AI reshapes value creation, competitive advantage, and human roles in digital commerce. The paper concludes by identifying open research challenges and future directions for responsible adoption of agentic commerce in high-frequency retail environments.

title: Lar Framework: Deterministic Metacognition and Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) Integration
abstract: This preprint formally defines the theoretical foundation and architectural primitives of the Lár Engine, an open-source (Apache 2.0) deterministic graph-state orchestration framework designed to resolve the autoregressive unpredictability and catastrophic forgetting inherent in standard Large Language Model (LLM) agents. We formally classify the Lár Node Ecosystem, including generative (LLMNode), computational (ToolNode), conditional (RouterNode), scaling (BatchNode/ReduceNode), and regulatory (HumanJuryNode) primitives, which enforce absolute execution constraints via a proprietary JSON Blueprint grammar. Furthermore, this publication establishes explicit prior art for two novel orchestration paradigms: 1. Structured Metacognition & Fractal Agency: The theoretical formulation of self-evaluating autonomous loops (HallucinationDetectorNode, SelfAwarenessNode) operating identically to an external prefrontal cortex, scoring generative outputs against rigid environmental telemetry prior to state mutation. It additionally defines the mathematical basis for Fractal Agency (DynamicNode), enabling agents to recursively synthesize, validate, and spawn isolated sub-graph topologies at runtime. 2. Lár-JEPA (Prediction via Embedding Space): The theoretical adaptation of Yann LeCun's Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture explicitly for deterministic graph orchestration. By shifting the computational burden from generative token prediction to the routing of high-dimensional latent state embeddings (System 2 routing), the framework executes safety vetoes and abstract action simulation before interacting with a physical environment. This document serves as permanent, cryptographic prior art establishing Aadithya Vishnu Sajeev as the sole inventor of these advanced architectural methodologies within the snath-ai/lar and snath-ai/lar-JEPA ecosystems.

title: AI Innovation in Business
abstract: Unlike many AI books that take a purely technical or cheerleading angle, this book bridges strategy, management, technology, and policy to demystify the AI revolution and tackle the urgent question facing today’s leaders: How can we truly unlock value from AI? Championing an ecosystem approach, Jonny Holmström reveals that capturing AI’s full value is not just a technical hurdle but a strategic and organizational challenge that demands new ways of thinking and collaborating beyond the walls of any single company. Readers will discover how an ecosystem approach – coordinating efforts across departments, companies, and even industries – can turn isolated AI experiments into transformative business value. Blending real-world case studies, cutting-edge research, and pragmatic frameworks, the book provides a roadmap to sustainable AI innovation, from preparing your organization for AI (“AI readiness”) to forging data strategies and addressing ethical dilemmas. For business leaders, IT professionals, and policymakers alike, this is essential reading for those looking to harness AI’s potential responsibly and strategically—not merely as a tool, but as a catalyst for reinventing the future of business.

title: Sentiment Optimization of GPT Text Generation Based on the Combination of New Reward Function and Hyperparameter Strategy
abstract: With the wide application of Large Language Models (LLMs) in the field of natural language processing, controlling the emotional tendency of generated text to meet human values or specific application scenario requirements has become a current research hotspot. However, existing Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) methods often face problems such as poor stability and easy model collapse during training, and the fixed KL divergence penalty coefficient makes it difficult to achieve a dynamic balance between exploring new strategies and maintaining language fluency. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a fine-tuning framework optimized using the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm, aiming to guide GPT models to generate Chinese text with positive emotions. By fine-tuning the JD sentiment classification model, an emotion discriminator highly adapted to the domain is constructed. Meanwhile, we combine it with the proportion of positive sentences in each batch to implement a new reward function, which can provide more accurate and robust emotional tendency reward signals for generated text. This method not only improves the discrimination accuracy of the reward function in the Chinese context but also provides a stable and interpretable optimization direction for subsequent reinforcement learning training. To further enhance training efficiency and model stability, we innovatively combine the cosine annealing learning rate adjustment strategy with the linear KL decay mechanism: the cosine annealing strategy effectively avoids the model falling into local optima by periodically adjusting the learning rate; while linear KL decay gradually reduces the regularization intensity of strategy updates during training, balancing exploration and exploitation, enabling the model to steadily approach the optimal strategy while maintaining diversity. Experimental results show that the proposed method is significantly superior to the baseline model in terms of sentiment consistency and text fluency, with the sentiment accuracy improved by approximately 16.2%, fully verifying the effectiveness and advancement of the proposed training framework.

title: Optimized QA Systems with Layered Search and Adaptive Query Refinement
abstract: As computer programs that use intelligence get bigger there is a growing need for systems that can answer tough questions with information that is current and based on the context. Something that systems that do not change cannot provide. Systems that are trained on fixed sets of data tend to make things up give answers or fail when questions need answers from more than one document. To fix these problems we built a system called Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering that combines three parts: a search engine that uses both keywords and complex math, a network that checks how well the answers fit the context and a module that refines the questions. The search engine uses both keywords and complex math to find the information without missing important details. The answers it finds are then checked by the network to see how well they fit the context not just how similar they are. Then the question is rewritten if it does not work well. The system can find better information next time. This helps reduce the number of made-up answers makes the answers more accurate and makes it clearer how the system got the answer.We tested our system on Natural Questions and TriviaQA. Two tests that check how well systems can answer questions on any topic. And found that it worked better than other systems even when the questions got harder. Our system is made to be flexible and easy to understand which makes it a good choice for tools that academics use systems that companies use to manage knowledge and any situation where it is important to get the answers. The system is made of parts that work together which makes it easy to use in different situations. We think this is important because answer reliability matters. Our Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering system is a choice when you need to get the right answers. We like our Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering system because it is good at answering questions. The system is good at finding the information and giving accurate answers. Our Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering system is a tool, for anyone who needs to answer questions.

title: RTL to GDSII Implementation of Lightweight IOT Authentication Hardware using Multifunction Residue-Based Cryptographic Architectures
abstract: Internet of Things (IOT) devices need to be secure and should be of low energy consumption. In terms of security, a lightweight hardware-based cryptography method is used. In the existing methods, it consumes more power due to continuous clock switching. This paper proposes a low-power hardware authentication encoder. In order to reduce dynamic power consumption due to unwanted clock switching in the system, clock gating is used at the architectural level. This clock gating uses an enable signal to reduce clock switching. This enable signal will be active only when necessary. This clock will propagate and reduce the power consumption in the system. The proposed design includes an ALU, a 63-bit LFSR, and a carry look-ahead adder. The design is verified, and it shows that the design uses low power consumption compared to other existing designs.

title: Analysing Lightweight Large Language Models for Biomedical Named Entity Recognition on Diverse Ouput Formats
abstract: Despite their strong linguistic capabilities, Large Language Models (LLMs) are computationally demanding and require substantial resources for fine-tuning, which is unadapted to privacy and budget constraints of many healthcare settings. To address this, we present an experimental analysis focused on Biomedical Named Entity Recognition using lightweight LLMs, we evaluate the impact of different output formats on model performance. The results reveal that lightweight LLMs can achieve competitive performance compared to the larger models, highlighting their potential as lightweight yet effective alternatives for biomedical information extraction. Our analysis shows that instruction tuning over many distinct formats does not improve performance, but identifies several format consistently associated with better performance.

title: Simulation-based Inference towards Gravitational-wave waveform systematics in Intermediate-Mass Binary Black Holes
abstract: Parameter estimation for gravitational-wave signals is computationally demanding due to the high dimensionality of the parameter space and the cost of repeated waveform generation in traditional Bayesian inference. These analyses require on the order of 10^8 likelihood evaluations and waveform generations, resulting in inference times of hours to days per event. Furthermore, discrepancies between waveform models introduce systematic uncertainties that can bias inferred source properties. To address these challenges, we propose a novel framework based on Simulation-based Inference (SBI) and Neural Posterior Estimation (NPE) and apply it to signals from Intermediate-Mass Black Holes (IMBH). In this framework, we train a single amortised neural posterior estimator on a large simulated dataset generated using two state-of-the-art waveform approximants, IMRPhenomXPHM and SEOBNRv5PHM. By treating the waveform model index as a latent variable, the network learns to produce posterior distributions that are naturally marginalized over the discrepancies of the two waveform models. Once trained, the model enables direct posterior sampling in milliseconds per event, eliminating the need for likelihood evaluations while simultaneously accounting for model systematics. We demonstrate that this approach recovers accurate posterior distributions for IMBH signals injected into Gaussian noise, achieving close agreement with traditional nested-sampling results while reducing inference time by several orders of magnitude. Our results show that NPE can robustly incorporate waveform-model systematics within a unified framework, offering a scalable path toward rapid, systematics-aware gravitational-wave inference. Establishing these methods as promising alternatives to classical likelihood-based pipelines for current and future high-mass gravitational-wave observations.
